The present Criminal Revision Petition (No. 378/2017) arises from the impugned order dated 14.02.2017 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Pali, in Case No. 05/2016, whereby the learned (Uploaded on 10/10/2025 at 10:34:40 AM) [2025:RJ-JD:43547] (2 of 7) [CRLR-378/2017] trial court discharged the petitioners from the offence under Section 406 IPC, but proceeded to frame charges against them under Sections 498A and 306 IPC.

1.1. Simultaneously, Criminal Revision Petition No. 503/2017 has been preferred by the complainant Mohd. Aslam, praying for further framing of charge under Sections 498A and 306 IPC against the accused-respondents.

2. Briefly stated the facts of the case are that on 31.05.2015, the complainant Mohd. Aslam lodged a written report alleging that his cousin sister, Smt. Ruksana, was married to petitioner No.3 Anwar Ali on 23.06.2002.
After marriage, she was allegedly subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws (petitioners No.1 and 2) on account of dowry.
Despite repeated reconciliations attempted by her family, the harassment continued.
2.1. The complainant alleged that she was once expelled from her matrimonial home and stayed with her parents for about five months.
Later, she was taken back by her in-laws, but the cruelty persisted.
2.2. On 31.05.2015, Ruksana sustained severe burn injuries at her matrimonial home after pouring kerosene on herself.
She was admitted to Bangad Hospital and later referred to Jodhpur, where she succumbed.
Initially, an FIR was registered under Sections 498A and 307 IPC; upon her death, the offence was altered, and a charge-sheet was filed under Sections 498A, 406, and 306 IPC.
(Uploaded on 10/10/2025 at 10:34:40 AM)
The learned trial court vide order dated 14.02.2017 discharged the accused from Section 406 IPC, but framed charges under Sections 498A and 306 IPC.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the deceased, who died of burn injuries after pouring kerosene upon herself, had committed suicide on her own volition and without any abetment on the part of the accused.
It was urged that the petitioners have been falsely implicated and that the prosecution material, even if taken at its face value, is insufficient to warrant framing of charges.

Counsel further submitted that the allegations of cruelty are omnibus and vague in nature,
lacking the specificity required to constitute an offence under Section 498A IPC.

With regard to Section 306 IPC, it was argued that in the absence of any positive act of instigation, provocation, or intentional aid attributed to the petitioners, the basic ingredients of abetment of suicide are not made out, and therefore, the trial court erred in proceeding to frame charges under both Sections 498A and 306 IPC.
4.

Conversely, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the revision and submitted that the deceased died an unnatural death within her matrimonial home, otherwise than in normal circumstances, by way of burning.

It was contended that the statements of prosecution witnesses, coupled with the surrounding circumstances have clearly disclosed a prima facie case of persistent cruelty and harassment meted out by the petitioners to the deceased, which ultimately drove her to commit suicide.

sentences.text:
The learned Public Prosecutor emphasized that at the stage of framing of charge,
the Court is not required to critically appreciate the evidence or assess the defence version; rather,
the limited enquiry is confined to determine whether a prima facie case exists, and in this backdrop,
the trial court has rightly framed the charges.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone through the impugned order as well as other material placed on record.
5.1. It is undisputed that the deceased died within her matrimonial home in unnatural circumstances, due to burning.
5.2. The allegations of persistent cruelty and harassment prima facie disclose commission of an offence under Section 498A IPC.
Further, when such cruelty is alleged to have continued till shortly before her death, it raises a grave suspicion of abetment sufficient to justify framing of charge under Section 306 IPC as well.
5.3. At the stage of framing charge, the law is well settled that the Court is not to conduct a roving enquiry or embark on a meticulous appreciation of evidence.
The defence cannot be weighed at this stage.
The only requirement is whether the material discloses grave suspicion of commission of the alleged offences or not.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kanti Badrusha v. State of West Bengal [2001 (1) SCR 27] has held that at the charge- framing stage, it is not necessary for the trial court to record elaborate reasons or to undertake detailed appreciation of evidence.

entities.text: Kanti Badrusha v. State of West Bengal [2001 (1) SCR 27]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.5. It is also well established that the revisional jurisdiction of this Court is narrow and limited.
Interference is warranted only in cases of patent illegality, gross perversity, or miscarriage of justice.

This Court cannot substitute its own view for that of the trial court merely because another interpretation of the evidence is possible.
6.
In the present case, the learned trial court has examined the material on record and found cogent reasons to frame charges under Sections 498A and 306 IPC against the petitioners.

No perversity,
illegality, or material irregularity is found in the impugned order.
The arguments raised on behalf of the petitioners essentially call for a deeper appreciation of evidence, which is impermissible at this preliminary stage.

7. For the reasons recorded hereinabove, this Court is satisfied that the learned trial court has rightly framed charges against the petitioners under Sections 498A and 306 IPC, after discharging them from Section 406 IPC.
8.
Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Petition No. 378/2017 filed by the petitioners is dismissed.
The stay petition and all pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

sentences.text: The petitioner complainant-Mohd. Aslam has preferred the present petition assailing the order dated 14.02.2017 passed by the learned trial court whereby charges came to be framed against accused respondents under Sections 306 and 498A IPC.

The grievance projected by the complainant is that the trial court erred in not framing charges against accused-respondent No.2 & 3 being father-in-law and mother-in-law under Sections 304B and 406 IPC.
2.

It is trite law that in order to attract Section 304B IPC (dowry death), the prosecution must establish the following ingredients:
1.The death of a woman occurred otherwise than under normal circumstances.
2.Such death occurred within seven years of her marriage.
3.It must be shown that soon before her death, the woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives in connection with demand for dowry.

In the present case, while it is alleged that the deceased died under circumstances not normal, it is an admitted position on record that the unfortunate incident occurred beyond seven years from the date of marriage.
The statutory prescription under Section 304B IPC that the death should occur within seven years of marriage is a mandatory precondition.

Since this requirement is not fulfilled,
the essential ingredients of Section 304B IPC are absent.

Consequently, no charge under Section 304B IPC could be legally sustained against the accused Nos.2 and 3.
(Uploaded on 10/10/2025 at 10:34:40 AM) [2025:RJ-JD:43547] (7 of 7) [CRLR-378/2017]
3.

The gravamen of an offence under Section 406 IPC (criminal breach of trust) lies in the element of entrustment of property, followed by dishonest misappropriation, conversion, or refusal to return the entrusted property.
In the present case, the record is bereft of any specific averment or prima facie evidence of entrustment of any property to the father-in-law or mother-in-law of the deceased.
Nor is there any allegation of dishonest misappropriation or wrongful retention on their part.
In absence of these foundational facts, the invocation of Section 406 IPC is wholly unwarranted.
4. Thus, upon a holistic consideration of the factual matrix and legal position, it is clear that the ingredients of Sections 304B and 406 IPC are not satisfied on the present record.
The learned trial court, therefore, committed no error in confining the charges to Sections 306 and 498A IPC against the accused persons.
5. Accordingly, the challenge laid by the complainant is found to be devoid of merit and stands dismissed.
All pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

(FARJAND ALI),J 30-Mamta/-
